new_candidates.duration: From adoption (immediate effect) through a fixed sunset of November 18, 2026, or the effective date of a zoning ordinance amendment addressing data centers, whichever occurs first
new_candidates.legal_basis: Resolution No. 26-07-04R, 'A Temporary Resolution Establishing a Moratorium on Issuance of Local Permits for Data Centers Within the City of Aberdeen,' adopted 7-0 at a regular Aberdeen City Council meeting on 2026-07-20, under authority of SDCL Sec. 49-50-3 (effective 2026-07-01)
new_candidates.trigger: City's current zoning/building regulations and staff may not adequately address data centers; council found officials 'hampered' in assessing permit applications, creating unpredictability and risk of stranded investment pending a comprehensive study
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23. Resolution 26-07-04R (adopted 7-0 on July 20, 2026, published July 23, 2026) bars Aberdeen zoning and building officials from issuing any permit or license for the construction, development, or operation of a data center within city limits; any pending application is held without review or action. The resolution took immediate effect as an emergency measure under SDCL Sec. 9-19-13 and automatically expires and is repealed on November 18, 2026, or on the effective date of a zoning-ordinance amendment (Aberdeen City Code Chapter 60 - Zoning) addressing data centers, whichever is first. As of September 22, 2026, the City Attorney was still briefing the council on the timeline for that follow-on zoning ordinance, which had not yet been adopted.
new_candidates.affected_projects: None named; as of publication Aberdeen had not received a specific data center development proposal for City Council consideration.
new_candidates.outcome: Adopted 7-0 on first reading and passage at the July 20, 2026 regular City Council meeting; published July 23, 2026.

OKs Wind Farm Pause,' dated on or about 2025-08-27/28) that the Turner County Commission enacted a one-year moratorium on wind energy projects, putting the proposed Swan Lake Wind development on hold. Turner County Board of Adjustment minutes from 2025-09-23 confirm the Commission had adopted a 'Moratorium on Solar and Wind Energy Systems' ordinance and that the Board discussed forming a task force on it; minutes from 2025-10-21 show continued discussion of the 'Solar/Wind moratorium.' A public-notice listing indicated Turner County scheduled an 8:35 a.m. public hearing on 2026-08-25 in Parker to consider extending a 'temporary moratorium on utility-scale alternative energy systems' county-wide, but the archived copy of that notice did not retain the underlying notice text (JS-rendered page returned only site boilerplate) and the outcome of any such hearing could not be confirmed from a source with retrievable primary text as of 2026-09-23.

new_candidates.duration: One year from its December 12, 2024 effective date; extended unanimously on October 21, 2025 through November 18, 2026
new_candidates.legal_basis: Pennington County Board of Commissioners temporary zoning moratorium on utility-scale wind and solar development, adopted unanimously November 19, 2024 (effective December 12, 2024); extended unanimously October 21, 2025 through November 18, 2026, while an alternative-energy task force and the Planning Commission draft amendments to zoning ordinance Section 3-17 (renewable energy systems)
new_candidates.trigger: More than 450 citizens petitioned for a moratorium after the Planning and Zoning Commission approved conditional-use permits (2024-10-28) for the Cheyenne River Ranch Wind and Solar Farm near New Underwood
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23. Pennington County's temporary zoning moratorium on utility-scale wind and solar development (enacted unanimously November 19, 2024, effective December 12, 2024, after 450+ citizens petitioned against the Cheyenne River Ranch Wind and Solar Farm's conditional-use permits) was extended unanimously by the Board of Commissioners on October 21, 2025 through November 18, 2026, to give an alternative-energy task force (formed March 2025) and the Planning Commission time to finish a consolidated ordinance amending zoning Section 3-17. A related but legally separate zoning-ordinance amendment permanently barring utility-scale wind and solar from agricultural (non-industrial) land passed its second and final reading 3-2 on August 18, 2026, after a multi-month back-and-forth (first reading May 19, 2026; delayed multiple times); commissioners indicated the moratorium could be lifted early once the Planning Commission's consolidated ordinance is finalized.
new_candidates.affected_projects: Cheyenne River Ranch Wind and Solar Farm (7 miles south of New Underwood, 30 miles southeast of Rapid City), which received conditional-use permit approval October 28, 2024 that triggered the petition and moratorium.
new_candidates.outcome: Extended by unanimous vote (moved by Commissioner Durr, seconded by Commissioner Rosknecht) at the October 21, 2025 Board of Commissioners meeting.

evidence.quote: The county imposed an initial moratorium on Nov. 19, 2024, while a task force drafted changes to Section 3-17 of the zoning ordinance covering renewable energy systems. That temporary moratorium was set to expire in December 2025. ... The board ultimately approved a one-year extension of the temporary zoning ordinance.

evidence.title: County bars utility wind and solar from agricultural land (3-2 vote from Pennington County Commission final step in barring utility-scale green energy projects on ag land)
evidence.supports: Confirms the separate permanent zoning-ordinance amendment barring utility-scale wind/solar from agricultural land passed its final 3-2 vote on August 18, 2026, and provides an embedded timeline confirming the November 19, 2024 moratorium enactment, December 12, 2024 effective date, and October 21, 2025 extension to November 18, 2026 (timeline text is ROT47-obfuscated in the page's HTML per known Lee Enterprises/BLOX CMS behavior and was decoded to confirm these dates).
evidence.quote: Nov. 19, 2024: Commission votes unanimously to enact a year-long moratorium on all utility-scale wind and solar projects in the county. Dec. 12, 2024: Moratorium goes into effect. ... Oct. 21, 2025: Commission votes unanimously to extend the moratorium to Nov. 18, 2026.

new_candidates.notes: The Nov. 19, 2024 enactment predates this sweep's usual since-2026-08-01 window but is included per the process doc's allowance for 'older ones the inventory missed,' since the moratorium remains active through Nov. 18, 2026 and was substantively extended within the window (Oct. 21, 2025). Distinct from the permanent zoning-ordinance amendment barring wind/solar from agricultural land (final vote Aug. 18, 2026), which is a separate, non-time-limited instrument and not itself recorded as a moratorium candidate.
